landing.hero.headline: Walk the cooler way.
landing.hero.subline: Oasyn Maps finds walking routes with less sun, more shade, and cooling nearby.
landing.features.title: What it does
landing.feature.1.title: Routes by heat, not just time
landing.feature.1.body: Compare routes on modeled sun exposure, shade, and cooling access.
landing.feature.2.title: Honest labels
landing.feature.2.body: Modeled and simulated values are always marked as such.
landing.feature.3.title: Cooling nearby
landing.feature.3.body: See cooling centers, water, and parks along the way.
landing.feature.4.title: Sun mode
landing.feature.4.body: A high-contrast layout for reading the screen in glare.
landing.feature.5.title: A lab to explore
landing.feature.5.body: Change the weather, play back a walk, and watch the model respond.
landing.feature.6.title: Private by default
landing.feature.6.body: No account. Your id stays on your device.
landing.how.title: How it works
landing.how.step1: Set a start and a destination.
landing.how.step2: Compare routes by modeled heat and shade.
landing.how.step3: Walk, and get offered a cooler route if things change.
landing.honesty.title: Data and honesty
landing.honesty.body: Exposure is modeled, not measured. Safety and wearable features are simulated for the demo.
landing.whoFor.title: Who it is for
landing.whoFor.body: People who walk in hot cities: commuters, caregivers, outdoor workers, and visitors.
landing.kiro.title: Built with Kiro
landing.kiro.body: Specs, steering, hooks, and the CLI guided this build.
landing.kiro.spec: Spec: requirements, design, and tasks drove each hour.
landing.kiro.steering: Steering: always-on rules for the UI, i18n, and safety.
landing.kiro.hooks: Hooks: content and i18n checks ran on save.
landing.kiro.cli: CLI: the build, tests, and gates ran from one command.

consent.emergency: The emergency flow is simulated. No call is ever placed.
about.title: About
about.body: Oasyn Maps is a prototype exploring heat-aware walking navigation.

coverage.intro.body: How far people here have to walk to reach somewhere to cool down: a cooling centre, a water fountain, or a shady park.
coverage.stat.within5: of the area is within a 5-minute walk of cooling
coverage.stat.within10: of the area is within a 10-minute walk of cooling
coverage.map.title: Where access is good or poor
coverage.suggestions.title: Best places for a new cooling spot
coverage.suggestions.body: A new cooling spot at these places would shorten the walk to cooling for the most people.
coverage.saves: Cuts about {minutes} of walking, added up across all nearby streets
coverage.none: No new spots are needed here right now.
coverage.how.title: How to read this
coverage.how.step1: We check every street corner for its walking time to the nearest cooling spot.
coverage.how.step2: Higher percentages mean more of the area can reach cooling quickly.
coverage.how.step3: Suggested spots show where a new cooling site would help the most.
departure.intro.body: We check the same walk at different times of day. As the sun moves, shade changes, so some start times are much cooler than others.
departure.empty.title: Pick a trip first
departure.empty.body: Set a start and a destination on the map, or try a sample trip, and we will find the coolest time to go.

departure.chart.title: Heat on this walk through the day
departure.list.title: Every start time we checked
departure.tip: Heat-minutes are the minutes of your walk spent in strong heat. Lower is better.
